mission: Ben first tries the ordinary Jedi path during the collapse. It is too slow. Remembering Iressa emotionally rather than philosophically, he acts decisively with Jacen-shaped crisis clarity and saves lives. Some people are grateful; some are shaken by how it felt to be moved or commanded.
why_now: Tavi is chest-deep and the scaffold above him is failing — Ben has minutes, and the ordinary approach (coordinating shouted instructions across flooding chaos) is going to cost Tavi his life before it finishes. The rescue has become a precision problem.
conflict: The ordinary Jedi approach — wait, coordinate, trust people to follow clear instructions — is not fast enough for a panicking person in rising cold water with broken scaffold overhead. Ben can see the solution Jacen’s crisis logic offers. Using it is choosing a method he has never let himself use on a person.
turning_point: Aevyn recognizes the pattern: Jacen taught Ben that.
closing_hook: Aevyn recognizes the pattern: Jacen taught Ben that.
setting: Iresh, the Glasswell main chamber and the equipment-staging shelf — now actively collapsing. Water at the knees by the time Ben reaches the main chamber; rising to chest by the end. Ceiling cracking in three places, stone falling in steady curtains. The scaffold ring is twisted and half-submerged. Tavi is trapped against a fallen scaffold near the basin's far wall.
emotional_trajectory: Rescue first, duel second. Ben’s dangerous choice must come from compassion and urgency, not aggression. The rescue should be clearly heroic before it becomes unsettling. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: The reader must understand why the ordinary rescue fails: water, blocked routes, panic, collapsing supports, Tavi’s time running out. Ben sees bodies, exits, water, weight, and panic the way Jacen taught him to see crisis.

stakes.personal: Ben uses the crisis perception Jacen trained in him — narrowing to bodies, exits, timing, weight, water level, falling stone, and panic vectors — and it works. He hates that it works as cleanly as it does. Iressa’s death surfaces not as a thought but as a physical memory: the moment he chose not to act, and what it cost.
stakes.interpersonal: After Ben uses the Jacen-shaped command clarity to direct Tavi through the last twenty meters of flooded passage, Tavi is alive and shaking and looks at Ben with an expression that is not gratitude — it is something quieter and more unsettled. Some of the Foundation’s trapped survey workers have the same look. They were moved, efficiently, by someone who did not ask.
stakes.external: The rescue leaves Aevyn uncontested on the upper platform with the holocron container. Every second Ben spent in the lower basin is a second Aevyn had to complete the opening and confirm what the holocron contains.

sensory_details: Rising water that smells of Iresh sediment and old mineral — not sea-water, colder, with something beneath the cold that does not have a name. The scaffold above Tavi groans with each new crack in the mineral shelf. Ben can hear where the structure is failing by the pitch of the groan. He noticed that without meaning to. He is grateful and ashamed of the gratitude.

turning_point_detail.trigger: The ordinary rescue approach has saved two people in five minutes; Tavi has thirty seconds before the scaffold drops. Ben stops asking Tavi to follow instructions and shifts to directing — a GAG-derived command clarity that does not manipulate Tavi's mind but uses the same crisis-perception framework to move people efficiently with minimal input from them. It is not a Force mind-trick. It is what Jacen taught him about control of a panicked space.
turning_point_detail.shift: Tavi is out of the water and alive. Aevyn, watching from the upper platform with the container, says: 'He taught you that.' It is not an accusation. It is a confirmation that what Ben just used is recognizable Jacen-derived method, and Aevyn recognizes it because he practiced the same framework.
turning_point_detail.cost: Several of the people Ben saved look at him the way they would look at someone who moved them without asking. Not injured — but handled. The distinction matters and Ben knows it.

emotional_arc.start: Ben begins the rescue trying to do it the right way — coordinated, voiced, patient — and it is failing. Tavi is running out of time. Ben does not let himself think about the other option; he acts.
emotional_arc.shift: The moment the Jacen-shaped clarity kicks in, Ben stops being conflicted and becomes effective. He is not happy about this. He is exactly as clear-eyed and decisive as Jacen taught him to be, and it works, and he has no room to examine what that means while Tavi is still alive to save.
emotional_arc.end: Tavi is out. Ben surfaces from crisis mode and Aevyn's words land in the quiet afterward. He taught you that. Yes. And it worked.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben tries the ordinary Jedi coordination approach for Tavi's rescue — shouted instructions, clear routes, patience — and it is too slow; the scaffold is failing and Tavi is panicking.
key_beats.state_change: The safe method is failing in real time; the gap between what the situation needs and what Ben has allowed himself to use becomes visible.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the specific frustration of a correct method not working; the other approach waiting at the edge of available thought

key_beats.beat_description: Ben shifts to Jacen-shaped crisis clarity without announcing it — narrowing to bodies, exits, timing, weight, moving people efficiently instead of asking them to follow.
key_beats.state_change: The rescue begins working; people are moving correctly without negotiation.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the clarity arriving as a physical sensation of focus; the discomfort of how clean it is, held in parallel rather than resolved

key_beats.beat_description: Tavi clears the water with seconds to spare before the scaffold section drops.
key_beats.state_change: The rescue succeeds within the constraint — Tavi is alive because Ben used the method he used.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the return of peripheral awareness after crisis narrowing; nothing triumphant, just the fact that it worked

key_beats.beat_description: Some of the rescued Foundation personnel look at Ben with disquiet — they were moved efficiently, and they noticed they did not choose to follow.
key_beats.state_change: The method's cost is visible in their faces — not injury, but the experience of being directed rather than asked.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the look landing; the distinction between saved and handled; no way to address it while the ceiling is still falling

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn, from the upper platform with the container: 'He taught you that.' Ben does not answer.
key_beats.state_change: Aevyn confirms that what Ben used is recognizable Jacen-derived method — and that Aevyn practiced the same framework.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the sentence arriving in the quiet after crisis; no defense available that would not be an admission
